identity.title: ALMA observations of the kinematics and chemistry of disc formation

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we present ALMA Early Science (Cycle 0) observations of deeply embedded protostars in the Corona Australis region

targets.name: R CrA IRS7B (plus CXO 34, IRS7A, SMM 1C)

evidence.quote: in the R CrA cloud (NGC 6729) within the Corona Australis star-forming region, one of the nearest star-forming regions, at a distance of 130 pc (cite: neuhauser08).

question.value: Is there a Keplerian disc around the Class 0/I protostar IRS7B in the R CrA cloud, and how does the disc relate to the presence of complex organic molecules in the inner envelope?

evidence.quote: We aim to better understand the structure of the inner regions of these protostars and, in particular, the interplay between the chemistry and the presence of discs.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00628.S.
R CrA IRS7B was observed on 4, 6, and 9 May 2012 in ALMA band 7 as part of ALMA Cycle 0 observations.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows, 336.955–349.814 GHz, 3840 channels each, 122 kHz (~0.11 km/s) channels

evidence.quote: The observations were performed in four spectral windows simultaneously (see Table [1](#tab:spw) for details), each with 3840 channels with channel widths of 122 kHz ($\sim0.11$ km s$^{-1}$).
18 antennas were part of the array, positioned in an extended configuration with baselines of 30–380 m (34–$430~\mathrm{k}\lambda$).
This resulted in a synthesised beam size of approximately $0.42\ensuremath{''}\times0.37\ensuremath{''}$ ($\mathrm{P.A.} \approx 72\ensuremath{^\circ}$).
The typical rms in line-free channels is 9–10 mJy beam$^{-1}$ channel$^{-1}$.
The total integration time of the observations was 5.5 hours.
R CrA IRS7B was observed on 4, 6, and 9 May 2012 in ALMA band 7
Single-dish observations of the region performed with the ASTE telescope show very strong CH$_3$OH emission (cite: watanabe12)

method.value: Fit strongest peak per channel in uv data, derive PA and PV diagram

evidence.quote: Through the CASA task `uvmodelfit` we identify the strongest peak of the C$^{17}$O emission in each channel of the $(u,\varv)$ data.

key_parameters.value: PA -65 deg, centre LSR velocity 6.2 km/s

evidence.quote: We find that the motion has a position angle of $-65$$^\circ$ on the sky and is centred around the channel corresponding to an LSR velocity of 6.2 km s$^{-1}$.

evidence.loc: Analysis, A Keplerian disc around IRS7B
evidence.quote: By the method of (cite: goodman93), which uses a weighted least-square fit to the positional data to establish the inclination of the velocity gradient on the plane of sky

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Keplerian disc with finite radius vs infall

method.value: Fit Keplerian profile plus linear branch; compare chi2 with v~r^-1 infall; compare against LIME fiducial disc

evidence.quote: by fitting a Keplerian profile (blue curve) and a straight line (green curve) to the data we can determine the disc radius very accurately.

key_parameters.value: free parameters: central mass and disc radius

evidence.quote: The central mass and the disc radius are the only free parameters.

assumptions.value: Flat disc, n∝r^-1, T∝r^-0.5, LTE, optically thin, inclination 60 deg

evidence.quote: the disc is assumed to be flat with a radial density profile $n(r) \propto r^{-1}$ and a temperature profile $T(r) \propto r^{-0.5}$.

fitting.value: chi2 fit weighted by uvmodelfit errors

evidence.quote: We do a $\chi^2$ fit to the velocities as a function of radius weighted by the `uvmodelfit` errors on the positional fits.

validation.value: Keplerian chi2 a factor 2.3 lower than infall

evidence.quote: the Keplerian fit has a $\chi^2$ value a factor 2.3 times lower than the infall fit

claims.hypothesis: C17O around IRS7B traces a Keplerian disc
claims.experiment: PV diagram from uvmodelfit peak positions, Keplerian vs infall fits
claims.result: Keplerian with edge at 50 AU, M*=2.3 Msun; chi2 2.3 times lower than infall
claims.finding: Keplerian disc favoured; infall not excluded

evidence.quote: the Keplerian model gives a better fit, in particular for the lower velocities, but the model with infall under conservation of angular momentum cannot be excluded

claims.hypothesis: A growing disc quenches complex organic chemistry in the inner envelope
claims.experiment: RATRAN CH3OH models with flat vs power-law inner density
claims.result: Flat inner density with abundance 1e-8 reproduces faint emission

evidence.quote: We propose that it has entered the stage where the disc dominates the physical and chemical structure at small radii.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Infall with angular momentum conservation considered, deemed unlikely due to sharp disc edge

evidence.quote: seems unlikely due to the well-defined edge of the disc which is observed.

limitations_admitted.value: Higher sensitivity and resolution needed to verify the Keplerian disc

evidence.quote: To verify that the C$^{17}$O emission on IRS7B originates in a Keplerian disc, higher-sensitivity and higher-resolution observations are needed.
